```bash
uv run python -m arena_kit.spec.lab build                                            # rebuild sheet + playbook
```

Each game uses one practice session. Without `--model` the games are code-only, which costs no model
credits and is repeatable. To test a new idea, add a variant to `VARIANTS` and `HYPOTHESES` and run it.
`spec.evaluate --no-learned` plays the defaults.

'''

The experiment loop is in the codebase and I ran it: **121 hosted practice games** in 6 batches. All ended in deals, with no errors and no contradicted claims. The agent now reads the results whenever it prepares a case, so `arena run --agent spec` uses them automatically.

**How it works**
- **The settings:** [strategy.py](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/spec/strategy.py) makes the main negotiating settings adjustable: how low to open, how fast to concede, and how close the supplier must come before we accept. Each named combination of settings is a "variant", with the hypothesis it tests written next to it. With no adjustments the agent behaves exactly as before.
- **The runner:** [lab.py](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/spec/lab.py) plays variants on the practice cases. Every game goes into the experiment sheet, `knowledge/experiments.jsonl` (also exported as `.csv`). It then rebuilds the result sheet [EXPERIMENTS.md](negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/knowledge/EXPERIMENTS.md) and `learned_playbook.json`, which the agent reads.
- **How the agent chooses:** it looks for evidence from the same case first, then cases of the same type and goal, then the same goal, then the same type. With nothing comparable it keeps the original settings. A variant is only used on a new case if it never lost any tested case badly.

**Results** (code-only games, so no model credits were used)

| Batch | Games | Mean score |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original settings | 10 | 0.665 |
| Agent using the learned picks | 10 | **0.703** |
| Each case treated as unseen | 10 | 0.665 |

- **P02:** 0.390 → 0.507, by holding out for a closer match before accepting. This matches the team's best.
- **P08:** 0.305 → **0.560**, by opening lower. This beats the team's best of 0.549.
- **P07:** 0.753 → 0.763, by opening lower and conceding faster.
- **P18:** 0.467 with the original settings, above the 0.453 target.
- **Rejected ideas:** opening close to the supplier's price lost 0.09 on average. Accepting early lost 0.045 on average.

**The limitation:** the "unseen" test is the honest guide to hidden final cases, and it scored the same as the original settings. That means it did no harm, but the gains didn't carry over. Each improvement so far is specific to one case, and with only 10 practice cases there aren't enough similar cases for a group pick to pay off. Two of the selection rules exist because the unseen test showed that looser rules would have cost P05 0.18 and P11 0.08.

**Also note:**
- All games were code-only. Your normal agent writes its e-mails with the model, and I haven't validated the picks in that mode. Doing so would use model credits.

- 221 tests pass and lint is clean. I added README and DESIGN_NOTES sections and made no commit.

To try a new idea, add a variant and its hypothesis in `strategy.py`, then run:

content.text:
The score did improve on the practice cases, from 0.665 to 0.703. What didn't improve is the "unseen case" test, which stayed at 0.665. There are three reasons, all visible in the game records.

**1. In 4 of the 10 cases the settings changed nothing.** All 10 variants produced the same result on P04 and P10, and 8 of 10 did on P01 and P03.
- **The supplier sets its own pace.** In P04 we opened at 4.49 with the original settings and 4.20 with the deep anchor. The supplier answered 4.94 → 4.90 → 4.89 (final offer) both times, so our opening made no difference.
- **The supplier ends the game early.** In P10 it sends a final offer after our first message, and we must accept or lose the deal. In P01 it said "agreed" after our second offer.
- **Our opening is capped by safety limits.** The agent never opens below the supplier's estimated full cost. In P01 and P03 that limit was already binding, so "open deeper" sent exactly the same first offer.

**2. The lost points are in the terms, not the price.** P01 shows this most clearly:

| | Price | Start date | Payment days | Score |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Our deal | **134.02** | Jan 2027 | 30 | 0.808 |
| Team's best run | 135.20 | Apr 2027 | 60 | **0.941** |

We got the lower price, but the earlier start and shorter payment terms cost about EUR 7,500 more overall. My settings only control the price path (how low to open, how fast to concede, when to accept). They don't control which terms the agent pushes for, and that's where P01, P03 and P05 lose most of their points.

**3. Gains on one case don't carry over to similar cases.** P08 and P18 are the same kind of case (raw material, leverage goal). Opening lower gained 0.255 on P08 but lost 0.081 on P18. With only 1–3 practice cases per group and results that point in opposite directions, the safety rule correctly refused to apply the gain to unseen cases. So unseen cases got the original settings.

**What would move the score:** experiments on the term choices themselves:
- which start date and payment days to ask for first;
- the order in which terms are negotiated;
- when to give up a term in exchange for price.

That needs a few new settings in the term-selection code (`steps.py` and `sheets.py`), then another sweep of about 40–60 games. 268 practice sessions are left. Should I build that and run it?

"""Settling the heavy terms one at a time (R13.1-R13.5), from the MESO agent - with its two failures
fixed (R13.3 reopen a costly lock, R13.4 a step needs a choice).

After coverage is set (R12.2) the remaining non-price terms are ranked by how many EUR they move C,
the playbook's terms first; terms under MIN_WEIGHT of C are skipped, at most MAX_STEPS are kept.
Each step message varies ONE term across up to three packages that all cost us the same C (R13.8);
the value the supplier answers with is locked and the next message varies the next term. When
every term is locked only price is left, and section 6's sheets take over.

Judgement call: payment days, when they are a step term, go first - so the first menu is also the
payment probe of R12.7 and message 1 varies a single term as R13.1 asks.
"""

from collections import Counter

from .estimate import RATE_BOUNDS
from .sheets import priced, structure_floor
from .terms import COVERAGE, complete, distance, key

MAX_STEPS = 3
MIN_WEIGHT = 0.002  # R13.1: a term that moves C by less than 0.2 % is not worth a round
REOPEN_SHARE = 0.01  # R13.3: a lock costing us 1 % of C against the term's best option is stepped again
MAX_PER_TERM = 2
STEP_SLACK = 0.004  # a package whose cheapest C is within 0.4 % of the target still counts as a choice


class Steps:
    """The step plan of one thread."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.order = None  # the terms worth a step, in order (fixed at the first move)
        self.weights = {}
        self.history = {}  # index of our message -> the term it varied, "price" or a one-off kind
        self.skipped = set()  # terms that had no credible choice (R13.4)
        self.revealed_values = {}

    # -- ranking ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def rank(self, ctx, base):
        """R13.1: the non-price, non-coverage terms by EUR weight, the playbook's first."""
        if self.order is not None:
            return self.order
        price = ctx.their_price
        c_base = ctx.c({**base, "unit_price": price})
        first = list((ctx.playbook or {}).get("first") or [])
        weights = []
        for f in ctx.case["negotiable"]:
            if f == "unit_price" or f in COVERAGE:
                continue
            opts = ctx.allowed(f, base)
            if len(opts) < 2:
                continue
            costs = [ctx.c({**base, f: o, "unit_price": price}) for o in opts]
            w = max(costs) - min(costs)
            if w >= MIN_WEIGHT * c_base:
                weights.append((w, f))
                self.weights[f] = w
        weights.sort(key=lambda x: (x[1] != "payment_days", first.index(x[1]) if x[1] in first else len(first), -x[0]))
        self.order = [f for _, f in weights[:MAX_STEPS]]
        return self.order

    # -- what is settled --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def counts(self):
        return Counter(v for v in self.history.values() if v not in ("price",))

    def locked(self, ctx, events):
        """After each step, the value of its term the supplier answered with (our first package's value
        if it answered without one, or with one that breaks a must-have). A term stepped only once whose
        answer costs us more than REOPEN_SHARE of C against its best option stays open (R13.3)."""
        out = {}
        mine = [i for i, m in enumerate(events) if m.get("from") == "buyer"]
        for k, field in sorted(self.history.items()):
            if field not in ctx.case["negotiable"] or k >= len(mine):
                continue
            i = mine[k]
            ours = ((events[i].get("term_sheets") or [{}])[0].get("terms") or {}).get(field)
            reply = next((m for m in events[i + 1 :] if m.get("from") != "buyer"), None)
            if reply is None:
                continue
            sheets = reply.get("term_sheets") or []
            theirs = sheets[0]["terms"].get(field, ctx.std.get(field, ours)) if sheets else ours
            out[field] = theirs if ctx.ok({**ctx.their, **out, field: theirs}) else ours
        counts = self.counts()
        t = complete(ctx.case, {**ctx.their, **out}, ctx.std)
        c_t = ctx.c(t)
        # an index clause is not reopened: the supplier that answers a deadband menu with its own clause
        # insists on it, and a second index menu drew holds and a final offer (P08, P18) - the rounds go
        # to price instead (MESO's P18: clause taken, price 5.60 -> 5.40)
        for field in [f for f in out if counts[f] == 1 and f != "index_clause"]:
            costs = [ctx.c({**t, field: o}) for o in ctx.allowed(field, t)]
            if costs and c_t - min(costs) > REOPEN_SHARE * c_t:
                del out[field]
        return out

    def revealed(self, ctx, latest_msg, alternatives):
        """R13.5: a term the supplier priced itself - its latest e-mail offers two packages that differ
        in that term only (its sheet and an alternative sheet or "Alternatively" line) - locked at the
        value that costs us less at the supplier's own prices."""
        sheets = [ts.get("terms") or {} for ts in latest_msg.get("term_sheets") or []]
        if not sheets:
            return dict(self.revealed_values)
        main = complete(ctx.case, sheets[0], ctx.std)
        best = {}
        for alt in [*sheets[1:], *alternatives]:
            full = complete(ctx.case, {**sheets[0], **alt}, ctx.std)
            diff = [f for f in ctx.case["negotiable"] if f != "unit_price" and key(full.get(f)) != key(main.get(f))]
            if len(diff) != 1 or diff[0] in COVERAGE or not ctx.ok(full):
                continue
            f = diff[0]
            choices = [(ctx.c(full), full[f])]
            if ctx.ok(main):
                choices.append((ctx.c(main), main[f]))
            choices += extrapolated(ctx, f, main, full)
            for c, value in choices:
                if f not in best or c < best[f][0]:
                    best[f] = (c, value)
        self.revealed_values.update({f: v for f, (_, v) in best.items()})
        return dict(self.revealed_values)

    def next_field(self, ctx, base, locked, asks=()):
        """The term this message varies: an asked-for step term first, else the next of the order that
        is not locked, not skipped and stepped at most once before; None once only price is left."""
        counts = self.counts()
        order = self.rank(ctx, base)
        for f in [*[a for a in asks if a in order], *order]:
            if f in locked or f in self.skipped or counts[f] >= MAX_PER_TERM:

            if len(ctx.allowed(f, base)) > 1:
                return f
        return None

    def only_price(self, ctx, base, locked):
        return self.next_field(ctx, base, locked) is None

    # -- the packages of one step -----------------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def option_order(ctx, field, base, asked=None):
        """R13.2: the best option for us first, then the one the supplier asked for, its current value,
        the middle option, the rest - three at most, each a different package."""
        opts = ctx.allowed(field, base)
        price = ctx.their_price
        theirs = complete(ctx.case, ctx.their, ctx.std).get(field)

input.content:
---
name: spec-agent-experiment-knowledge
description: Before changing SpecAgent strategy or building a new negotiation agent, read the experiment sheet in knowledge/ and use the lab with replay screening
metadata:
  type: project
---

SpecAgent learns from experiments (built 2026-10-11): `negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/knowledge/EXPERIMENTS.md` (result sheet), `experiments.jsonl` (every game), `learned_playbook.json` (read by the agent via `spec.strategy.choose`). Run the lab with `python -m arena_kit.spec.lab run --variants ... --sessions N`; it replays recorded games first, so only diverging games use practice sessions.

**Why:** the user wants every new agent and session to start from past experiments and not repeat mistakes. Practice sessions are scarce, and the user's own count of what is left can be lower than `arena me` reports (2026-10-11: user said 120, API said 268), so take the user's figure as the cap.

**How to apply:** read EXPERIMENTS.md before proposing strategy changes, add new ideas as named variants with a hypothesis in `spec/strategy.py`, test them via the lab with a `--sessions` cap, and check the leave-one-out (`learned --holdout`) result before claiming a gain on hidden cases. The hosted suppliers are deterministic for identical e-mails (code-only games repeat exactly), but the P05 RFQ depends on timing.

content.text:
I ran 47 more games and used **27 of your 40 sessions**; the replay screen played the other 20 for free. The agent's own picks now average **0.716**, up from 0.665 with the original settings, which matches the team's per-case targets on average. On cases treated as unseen it scores **0.682**, so some of the gain now carries over to new cases. Last time it didn't.

**What the new experiments found** (scores are code-only)

| Case | Original | Now | What fixed it |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| P01 | 0.808 | **0.859** | Move 20% toward a supplier's big step, not 50% |
| P02 | 0.390 | **0.507** | Hold out for a closer match before accepting |
| P08 | 0.305 | **0.593** | Deep opening + only one term menu, then price rounds |
| P18 | 0.467 | **0.513** | Only one term menu, then price rounds |
| P07 | 0.753 | 0.763 | Deep opening + faster concessions |

- **P01's real cause:** a "meet the supplier halfway" rule overrode every concession setting I'd tested before, and the supplier accepted that halfway offer immediately.
- **New default for unseen cases:** hold out for a closer match, plus only one term menu, then price rounds. It was the only variant that gained on three cases and lost none.
- **What didn't work:** changing the order in which terms are negotiated. The supplier's own request (payment days in P01) goes first anyway, and it answers every equal-cost menu in its own favour.

**Saving sessions:** the arena answers identical e-mails identically, so the lab now replays each game against the recorded ones and only uses a session when the agent writes something new. All 88 recorded games that could be replayed reproduced their exact scores. The one exception is P05, the three-supplier tender, which depends on reply timing and always needs a real session.

**Teaching new agents the old experiments:** yes, at three levels:
- **Every game:** the agent loads the learned playbook when it prepares a case and logs the matching lessons, for example "soft anchor lost −0.09 in leverage cases, avoid".
- **Every experiment:** old games are replayed instead of played again, and new real games are added to that replay record.
- **Future development sessions:** I saved a memory note telling them to read `knowledge/EXPERIMENTS.md` and use the lab before changing strategy. The README and DESIGN_NOTES describe the same workflow.

**Two things to check:**
- **Someone else ran the lab during my session.** A batch labelled `release-sunday-x2` used 8 more sessions (repeat games on P02, P05, P07 and P11). Its results match mine exactly, so I left them in the sheet. The arena now shows 233 sessions left. If you're tracking 120, that count may also include the other person's use.
- **Model mode is untested:** everything is still code-only. When the model writes the e-mails, the wording differs from game to game, so those games can't be replayed, and the picks are unconfirmed there.

223 tests pass and lint is clean. Nothing is committed, and the changes from before this session are still uncommitted alongside mine.

content.text:
No, nothing is hardcoded. Every score comes from the arena: when a game ends, the arena returns the deal, its total cost and the score, and the lab stores exactly that. The only fixed numbers in the code are the team's historical best scores in `evaluate.py`, used as targets in reports. They never feed into a result.

**You do get the same result when you play the same way.** In 21 cases where the same case was played with identical settings in separate real sessions, the score was identical every time. That happens for two reasons:
- **Our agent is deterministic in code-only mode.** With no model, the same situation always produces the same e-mail.
- **The arena's suppliers are deterministic too.** The same e-mail always gets the same reply, even in a new session. The arena's own documentation hints at this ("cached supplier responses").

Same e-mails in means same replies and the same score out.

**Different settings do give different scores:** P07 produced 9 distinct real-session scores across the variants, P18 7, P05 and P08 6 each. That's why the experiments measure something. In P03, P04 and P10 every variant scored the same, because the supplier controls the outcome there: it makes a final offer early or concedes on its own schedule.

**Be aware of three things:**
- **Replayed games are copies, not new measurements.** When the lab replays a game, it reuses the score the arena gave the identical recorded game. That's sound only because of the determinism above, but no new arena call happens. Each sheet row is flagged `replay: true` or false.
- **P05 is the borderline case.** Its repeats so far all scored the same (0.757 four times), but the agent's messages there depend on which of the three bidders answers first. So the replay can't reproduce it, and a real P05 game could in principle come out differently.
- **With the model on, results vary.** The model words each e-mail differently, so replies and scores differ from game to game. That's what your normal `--agent spec` runs use. The code-only experiments find good settings cheaply, but model-mode scores need several games per setting to average out.

So one code-only game per setting is a real measurement. Repeating it, as I did with the learned and holdout batches, confirms the score but tells you nothing new.

It's pushed to `feature/spec-agent` on GitHub as commit `dde8c9d`. All 223 tests passed before the commit.

What went in:
- **New code:** the strategy settings, the experiment lab and the replay screen, plus their tests and the README and DESIGN_NOTES updates.
- **The experiment knowledge:** the experiment sheet, the learned playbook and the result sheet (`knowledge/EXPERIMENTS.md`). The agent and any future session start from these.
- **The game records in `runs/lab/`** (about 7 MB). The replay screen needs them; without them, every experiment would cost real sessions again.
- **The earlier uncommitted work:** the tuning changes that were already in your working tree, such as the "supplier at its limit" close rule and the 0.98 anchor floor, plus four older run folders. My code builds on those changes, so they couldn't be left out.

Left out: `.DS_Store` and the cached quote PDFs. I added the PDF cache folder to `.gitignore`; the replay downloads those files from the old sessions when it needs them, without using a session.

Your git setup also pushed two "checkpoint" refs to `origin` along with the branch. That comes from the `entire` tool, not from this commit. If you don't want those refs on GitHub, check its settings.

I haven't opened a pull request. Should I open one against `main`?
